## Runs 6–7 — D = 0 SdH spot checks, raw → onset/FFT

Run 6: electron n = +3.2×10¹² cm⁻², 0→10 T, 10 mT above 1 T; run 7: hole n = −1.2×10¹² cm⁻², 10→0.3 T, 20 mT. Both use the run-5 calibration and the hardwired B₁–B₂ Rxx pair. Plot the raw, gain-divided drain current and Rxx before the frequency read.

from hera.analysis import open_run, plot_raw
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

r6, r7 = open_run('data/6'), open_run('data/7')
for r in (r6, r7):
    display(plot_raw(r))
    plt.close('all')

### SdH read and fan decision

The fixed-current Rxx estimate and the measured-current trace agree because drain current varies by <1% in each run. Sensitivity was 50 µV (≈5 kΩ at 10 nA); raw Rxx is −33…530 Ω (electron) and approximately 0…587 Ω (hole), with neither channel railing and gate-current extrema below 0.22 nA. The temperature logged 1.17–1.29 K. The electron run has a reproducible broad ≈7 T component and high-field ≈30 T structure; a 7 T comb/harmonic assignment remains possible, so this spot alone does not identify the stacking. The hole run has stronger low-frequency oscillations but is pinned to the model's near-CNP overlap exception and cannot span the design density. The onset tracker labels the 7.1 T electron component censored at 0.30 T; the resolved higher components appear at 1.36–1.91 T. Use B = 1.0–10 T for the fan, retaining the onset shoulder while sampling the full-density tone; this excludes sub-1 T content whose spot-check grid cannot resolve at F_L = 33 T. This is a coverage limit, not an absence claim.

from hera.analysis import sdh_onset, sdh_fft
from scipy.signal import find_peaks
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4), sharey=True)
for a, r, label in zip(ax, (r6, r7), ('electron +3.2', 'hole -1.2')):
    B = r.col('magnet_field')
    I = r.col('sr0_X') / -1e6
    R = r.col('sr1_X') / I
    on = sdh_onset(R, B, r_full_scale=50e-6 / 1e-8)
    print(f'run {r.path.name}: {on.summary()}')
    print(f'Rxx {np.nanmin(R):.1f}–{np.nanmax(R):.1f} Ω; I {np.nanmin(I)*1e9:.3f}–{np.nanmax(I)*1e9:.3f} nA; '
          f'T {np.nanmin(r.col("T_sample")):.3f}–{np.nanmax(r.col("T_sample")):.3f} K')
    for cutoff in (1., 1.5, 2., 2.5):
        f, S = sdh_fft(R[:, None], B, b_range=(cutoff, 10), nfft=1024, bg_degree=5, log=False)
        a.plot(f, S[0]/np.nanmax(S[0]), label=f'{cutoff:g}–10 T')
    a.set(xlim=(0, 45), ylim=(0, 1.1), xlabel='FFT frequency (T)', title=label)
    a.legend(fontsize=8)
ax[0].set_ylabel('normalized amplitude')
fig.tight_layout()
display(fig)
plt.close(fig)

## HERA — Step 4: D = 0 electron Landau fan (`landau-fan-vti`)

> **05:24** · D=0 electron Landau fan: n +3.2 to +2.7e12 (17), B 1->10 T uniform 1/B (91), sr1 50 uV, 1.8 s dwell; ends 10 T · **ETA ~07:49** (≈2h25m)

Runs 6–7 establish the side choice: run 6 at n = +3.2×10¹² has oscillations and a 7 T / high-field ≈30 T peak set whose harmonic origin needs an n-dependent read; run 7's hole side is limited to n ≥ −1.27×10¹², the model's near-CNP exception. Run-5 calibration gives D = 0 gate pairs from n = +3.2 to +2.7×10¹². The model predicts ABAB [7.31, 25.78] T at +3.2 and [5.72, 22.19] T at +2.7 versus ABCA F_L = 33.09 and 27.92 T. This fan will resolve the trajectory and test a single global density scale, the Luttinger sum, and harmonic/breakdown alternatives; the spot checks alone do not make a stacking call.

Use 91 field rows, **uniform in 1/B from 1 to 10 T**, and 17 paired gate points from n = +3.2 to +2.7×10¹² at D = 0. The 1/B step is 0.010 T⁻¹: 3.0 points per period at F_L(3.2) = 33.09 T, above the 2-point Nyquist floor. The n step is 0.03125×10¹² cm⁻², giving 3.1 points per g = 4 ray period at 1 T. The light ABAB model branch at the low-density edge has 5.15 periods across this field window; ideal δF = 1.11 T. The resolved high-frequency spot-check components appeared at 1.36–1.91 T, leaving δF ≈ 1.6–2.4 T even if their onset limits the usable record; the heavy-ABAB / ABCA separation of ≈5.7–7.3 T remains testable. **Coverage trade:** the fan excludes n < +2.7, where the light branch lacks five periods on this field span, and B < 1 T, where run 6's 7.1 T tracker is censored at the record edge and its coarse spot grid does not Nyquist F_L. No absence claim applies in those excluded regions.

The run starts from the handoff's 0 T, 0 V gates and positions to 1 T with a blocking ≈7.3 min ramp; it ends at 10 T for a possible measured ride-down later. Use run 6's 50 µV fixed Rxx sensitivity and 0.3 s / 24 dB filter; 1.8 s fast delay meets 6τ, with the magnet's 3 s settle on each field row. Full scale is ≈5 kΩ at 10 nA; run 6's raw high-field maximum was ≈530 Ω, giving headroom as density decreases to +2.7. Timing from runs 6/7: ≈66 min field traverse + 91×17×(1.8 s dwell plus ≈0.2–0.3 s gates/reads) + row settles and initial position, with ≈10% overrun allowance, ≈2 h 25 m. Before moving, the cell prints and asserts live thermometry, base T, 0 T, V_si = 0, and magnet heater/output. Check the first two complete rows for leakage, flat/railed Rxx, and gate tracking; then check again near 5 and 8 T for the low-n/high-B worst corner and use a partial frequency read if the signal warrants it. Abort a safety or acquisition failure; magnet ramp interruption is operator-side only.

# D = 0 electron Landau fan, first-session tetralayer FS-count arc.
from sharpelab_nb.gates import calc_gate_voltages, calc_nD

CAL = dict(c_tg=2.796e-03, c_bg=2.161e-03, n_offset=-0.0894, D_offset=-0.013)
ns = np.linspace(3.2, 2.7, 17)       # 1e12 cm^-2; n step 0.03125
Ds = np.zeros_like(ns)                # V/nm, D = 0
Vtgs, Vbgs = calc_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, CAL['c_tg'], CAL['c_bg'], CAL['n_offset'], CAL['D_offset'])
B_vec = 1 / np.linspace(1/1.0, 1/10.0, 91)  # uniform 1/B, 1 -> 10 T
assert np.all((TG_MIN <= Vtgs) & (Vtgs <= TG_MAX))
assert np.all((BG_MIN <= Vbgs) & (Vbgs <= BG_MAX))
assert B_vec.max() <= B_SESSION_CAP
assert np.allclose(calc_nD(Vtgs, Vbgs, CAL['c_tg'], CAL['c_bg'], CAL['n_offset'], CAL['D_offset'])[0], ns)
print(f'fan geometry: {len(B_vec)} B rows × {len(ns)} n points; B {B_vec[0]:.3f}->{B_vec[-1]:.3f} T, '
      f'n {ns[0]:.3f}->{ns[-1]:.3f}e12, D=0; Vtg {Vtgs[0]:+.4f}->{Vtgs[-1]:+.4f}, '
      f'Vbg {Vbgs[0]:+.4f}->{Vbgs[-1]:+.4f} V')

# Silent preconditions: this cell does not set T, Si, or PS/output state.
assert_thermometry_live('T_sample', VTI.temp_logfile_candidates['T_sample'], max_age=15, max_period=12)
_T0, _B0, _Si0 = T_sample(), magnet.field(), k_si()
_PS0, _out0 = magnet.persistent_switch_on(), magnet.output_enabled()
print(f'preconditions: T_sample {_T0:.3f} K [1.0,1.5], B {_B0:+.4f} T [|B|<0.05], '
      f'Si {_Si0:+.3f} V [|V|<0.01], PS heater {_PS0}, output {_out0}')
assert 1.0 <= _T0 <= 1.5 and abs(_B0) < 0.05 and abs(_Si0) < 0.01
assert _PS0 and _out0
assert TG_MIN == -0.3 and TG_MAX == 1.0 and BG_MIN == -1.3 and BG_MAX == 2.0
assert B_SESSION_CAP == 10.0 and T_SESSION_CAP == 100.0
assert abs(sr1.amplitude() - 1.0) < 0.01  # 10 nA nominal current bias
assert abs(sr1.time_constant() - 0.3) < 1e-6 and sr1.filter_slope() == 24

sr1.sensitivity(50e-6)  # fixed for the whole fan; 5 kOhm full scale at 10 nA
magnet.field(float(B_vec[0]))  # blocking position from 0 T; driver includes 3 s settle
s = sweep.AsyncStation(dict(meas_config, **{'Si (V)': _Si0, 'sample_temperature:': _T0,
    'comments': 'landau-fan-vti electron D=0, n +3.2 to +2.7e12, B 1 to 10 T uniform 1/B 91x17, run-5 calibration, sr1 50uV'}))
s.add_comment('landau-fan-vti')
s.add_comment('electron B1-B2 Rxx; n=+3.2 to +2.7e12 cm^-2, D=0 V/nm; '
              'B=1 to 10 T uniform 1/B (91 rows), 17 paired gate points; '
              'run-5 cal c_tg=2.796e-3, c_bg=2.161e-3, n_offset=-0.0894, D_offset=-0.013; '
              'sr1=50uV fixed, tau=0.3s/24dB, fast_delay=1.8s')
s.ramp(k_bg.volt, float(Vbgs[0])); s.ramp(k_tg.volt, float(Vtgs[0]))
interruptible_sleep(10)

# Row layout: time, B, Vtg, Vbg, T_sample, I_tg, I_bg, sr0.X/P, sr1.X/P.
s.fp(T_sample).fp(k_tg.curr).fp(k_bg.curr)
s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P)
s.plot('time', T_sample)
s.plot('time', k_tg.curr); s.plot('time', k_bg.curr)
s.plot(magnet.field, sr0.X); s.plot(magnet.field, sr0.P)
s.plot(magnet.field, sr1.X); s.plot(magnet.field, sr1.P)

def fan_leak_guard(station, data):
    i_tg, i_bg = abs(float(data[5])), abs(float(data[6]))
    if i_tg > 1e-9 or i_bg > 1e-9:
        print(f'LEAK TRIP B={float(data[1]):.3f} T, n-row Vtg={float(data[2]):+.4f}, '
              f'Vbg={float(data[3]):+.4f}: |I_tg|={i_tg:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg:.3e} A')
        station.interrupt_requested = True
s.register_run_after(fan_leak_guard, ())

s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs],
                 slow_delay=1.0, fast_delay=1.8)
print(f'fan done: B={magnet.field():+.3f} T, gates=({k_tg.volt():+.4f}, {k_bg.volt():+.4f}) V')
